ames_spectacles.name: Mr Ames's Spectacles
ames_spectacles.description: Mr Ames, at {place:ames}, has put his spectacles down in his garden and can't see to find them. He was looking at the beans, he said. He mostly looks at the road.
ames_spectacles.completion: They were on the path between the rows, folded, lenses down. He put them on and looked straight past me at the road.

requirements.text: His spectacles, in the garden at {place:ames}

tull_billhook.name: The Bill-hook
tull_billhook.description: Mr Tull cuts wood at {place:tull}. He put his bill-hook down in the clearing, turned round, and couldn't find it. He's been round the clearing twice and asked me to look.
tull_billhook.completion: It was in the clearing, stuck in the ground by its point. He said he never leaves it like that. He said it twice.

requirements.text: His bill-hook, in the clearing at {place:tull}

bettany_key.name: Locked Out
bettany_key.description: Mrs Bettany, at {place:bettany}, has locked herself out. The spare key is under a stone in her garden and she can't remember which. She'd been standing at her own door since the milk came.
bettany_key.completion: Under the third stone I turned. She let herself in and locked the door behind her while I was still on the step, then opened it again to say thank you.

requirements.text: Her spare key, in the garden at {place:bettany}

leckie_eggs.name: Eggs
leckie_eggs.description: Mrs Leckie, at {place:leckie}, says the hens have laid for the first time in a week. She asked me to fetch the eggs in from the hen house before anything else does.
leckie_eggs.completion: Three eggs, warm. She held each one up to the light before she put it in the bowl.

requirements.text: Eggs, from the hen house at {place:leckie}

leckie_barn.name: The Barn Door
leckie_barn.description: Mr Leckie went into the barn at {place:leckie} after his dinner and hasn't come out. Mrs Leckie won't knock. She asked me to knock, and to say it's only about his tea.
leckie_barn.completion: He answered through the barn door. He's counting the sacks, he said, and will be out when he's finished. Mrs Leckie says he's been counting them since March.

requirements.text: The barn door at {place:leckie}

leckie_sacks.name: Twelve Sacks
leckie_sacks.description: Mr Leckie counts eleven sacks of meal in the barn at {place:leckie}, and there should be twelve. Mrs Leckie knows the twelfth is in the sheep pen, where he put it himself on Sunday. She won't tell him so.
leckie_sacks.completion: Twelve. He counted them out loud, twice, and came out for his tea. Mrs Leckie gave me a jar from the pantry and didn't say what was in it.

requirements.text: The twelfth sack, in the sheep pen at {place:leckie}

rudd_bucket.name: A Bucket from the Well
rudd_bucket.description: Mrs Rudd, on the green at {place:rudd}, asked me to draw a bucket from the well. Her arms aren't what they were. She says the water has tasted of something since March, and wants somebody young to taste it.
rudd_bucket.completion: The water came up clear and very cold. It smelled of pennies. Mrs Rudd drank some and said that was it, that was exactly it.
rudd_bucket.returnTo: Mrs Rudd, on the green at {place:rudd}

requirements.text: The well on the green at {place:rudd}

rudd_next_door.name: Next Door
rudd_next_door.description: Mrs Rudd wants to know whether the water tastes of pennies next door too, at the next house along the green at {place:rudd}. She hasn't asked. Nobody on the green has been out much since March.
rudd_next_door.completion: Next door said yes, since March, and they drink it anyway, and would I please not knock after the bell. Mrs Rudd said nobody had said. Then she said she hadn't asked.
rudd_next_door.returnTo: Mrs Rudd, on the green at {place:rudd}

requirements.text: The next house along the green at {place:rudd}

kember_prints.name: Three Knocks
kember_prints.description: Mrs Kember, at {place:kember}, says somebody knocks at her door after the bell most nights, and when she looks there's nobody. She asked me to look for prints in the vegetable plot, where the ground is soft.
kember_prints.completion: No prints in the rows. There was a man's glove on top of the soil, dry, laid there that minute.

requirements.text: Prints, in the vegetable plot at {place:kember}

kember_glove.name: Whose Glove
kember_glove.description: Mrs Kember thinks she knows the glove and won't say. She asked me to take it to the next house along the green at {place:kember} and ask. She said to knock three times, and then she said not to.
kember_glove.completion: Next door took the glove through the gap of the chain and said it was his father's, and that his father went out one night in November to see who was knocking. Mrs Kember said she'd leave a light on tonight.

requirements.text: The glove, to the next house along at {place:kember}

pryor_sitters.name: Round the Cold Fire
pryor_sitters.description: Mr Pryor, who cuts at {place:pryor}, says men sit round a cold fire at {place:pryor_camp}, off the road, and have since the winter. He knew them. He wants them put down, gently, and doesn't want to hear how.
pryor_sitters.completion: They sat round a fire that hadn't been lit in a long while, and didn't get up until I was close. Mr Pryor thanked me and didn't ask anything.

requirements.text: The men round the cold fire at {place:pryor_camp}

gunn_bag.name: Left in the Yard
gunn_bag.description: Mr Gunn, who keeps {place:gunn}, has had a traveller's bag lying in the yard since Sunday and nobody has come for it. He asked me to bring it in. He'd rather not be the one to open it.
gunn_bag.completion: Nothing in it with a name. A shirt, a razor, and a ticket for the Sunday train, not punched.

requirements.text: The bag in the yard of {place:gunn}

gunn_room.name: Room Four
gunn_room.description: The traveller had the back room at {place:gunn}. Mr Gunn says he left his key on the barrels round the side every morning, and he wants it found so the room can be let.
gunn_room.completion: A key on a wooden tag, on top of the barrel: 4. Mr Gunn looked at it a while. He's got three rooms. He said he'd hang it on the board with the others.

requirements.text: The barrels at the side of {place:gunn}

hurst_fleece.name: Three Short
hurst_fleece.description: Mr Hurst, at {place:hurst}, is three sheep short in the pen. He thinks the lot camped at {place:hurst_camp}, off the road, had them. He wants to know for certain before he does anything he can't undo.
hurst_fleece.completion: There was fleece caught on a crate at their camp. Mr Hurst turned it over in his hands and said it was his mark, and that was that.

requirements.text: Any sign of his sheep at {place:hurst_camp}

hurst_camp.name: Moved On
hurst_camp.description: Mr Hurst wants the camp at {place:hurst_camp} moved on. He can't do it himself and there's nobody to send for. He said he was sorry to ask, and that he was at school with two of them.
hurst_camp.completion: It's quiet out that way. Mr Hurst didn't ask how. He gave me a jar his wife had put by for the winter.

requirements.text: The ruffians camped at {place:hurst_camp}

farrant_ring.name: The Crows' Place
farrant_ring.description: Mrs Farrant, at {place:farrant}, lost her ring out of the dish on the sill, and there was a crow at the window. She says the crows keep what they take at {place:farrant_camp}, off the road, and have for years.
farrant_ring.completion: It was in the chest at their place, with buttons, a thimble and a great many teaspoons. Mrs Farrant said the teaspoons weren't hers, and she wouldn't want them now if they were.

requirements.text: Her ring, where the crows keep things at {place:farrant_camp}

vosper_letter.name: The Post
vosper_letter.description: Mrs Vosper, at {place:vosper}, says the post has been left in her yard lately instead of at the door. There's a letter out there now. She asked me to bring it in. She doesn't go out to the yard.
vosper_letter.completion: A letter, dry, in her son's hand. She read it at the door and said he says the weather is fine and he'll be home on Sunday. She said he says that every week.

requirements.text: The letter in the yard at {place:vosper}

vosper_reply.name: Return of Post
vosper_reply.description: Mrs Vosper has written back, and asked me to take her letter to her sister at {place:vosper_sister}, down the road, who keeps them all. Her sister won't open the door. The letter goes through it.
vosper_reply.completion: It went in through the flap. From inside, her sister said thank you, and that she'd put it with the rest.

requirements.text: Her letter, through the door of {place:vosper_sister}

vosper_tin.name: In the Right Order
vosper_tin.description: Mrs Vosper wants her sister at {place:vosper_sister} to send back the tin of letters, all of them, his and hers. She didn't say why. She said it's time they were read in the right order.
vosper_tin.completion: Mrs Vosper sorted the letters on the table by their dates. The newest of her son's was older than the oldest of hers. She thanked me, and gave me something from the dresser that had been his.

requirements.text: The tin of letters, from {place:vosper_sister}

hackett_look.name: The House Off the Road
hackett_look.description: Mr Hackett, at {place:hackett}, grew up at {place:hackett_house}, off the road. It has no roof now. He asked me to look inside and tell him what's left. He hasn't been since, and he isn't going.
hackett_look.completion: Pencil marks up what was left of the door frame, names and heights. The last mark was higher than any of the others, and newer. Mr Hackett said that couldn't be right.

requirements.text: Inside the walls at {place:hackett_house}

hackett_tin.name: Under the Step
hackett_tin.description: Mr Hackett's mother kept a tin under the front step at {place:hackett_house}. He wants it, whatever is in it. He says he knows what's in it, and he'd still like it.
hackett_tin.completion: Buttons, a ration book in his mother's name, and a photograph of a house with a roof on it. He looked at the photograph a long time, and kept it.

requirements.text: The tin under the step at {place:hackett_house}

tobin_scissors.name: Her Scissors
tobin_scissors.description: Mrs Tobin, at {place:tobin}, left her scissors in the garden. She was cutting flowers when somebody on the road said her name. She came straight in and hasn't been out since. There was nobody on the road.
tobin_scissors.completion: The scissors were open on the path, and the flowers she'd cut lay in a row beside them, heads all one way. She said she hadn't laid them like that.

requirements.text: Her scissors, in the garden at {place:tobin}

venn_apples.name: Windfalls
venn_apples.description: Mrs Venn, at {place:venn}, has a bag of windfalls for the woodcutter at {place:venn_wood}, who cuts her wood and won't take money. She asked me to leave them on his woodpile. He won't stop work to be thanked.
venn_apples.completion: I left the apples on the woodpile. There was a bundle of kindling on it already, tied with green string. Mrs Venn said it was her string, and that she'd never given him any string.

requirements.text: Her apples, to the woodpile at {place:venn_wood}

denny_light.name: A Light in the Walls
denny_light.description: Mr Denny, who cuts at {place:denny}, has seen a light in {place:denny_ruin} from his clearing three nights running. Nobody has lived there for years. He asked me to look inside by day and tell him it's nothing.
denny_light.completion: Candle ends inside the walls, a great many, burnt down in saucers, and one kitchen chair facing the doorway. Mr Denny said that wasn't nothing, and then that it probably was.

requirements.text: Inside the walls at {place:denny_ruin}, by day

lusk_potatoes.name: Lifting
lusk_potatoes.description: Mr Lusk, at {place:lusk}, has potatoes to lift in his garden and a back that won't have it. He wants them up before the frost. He says the frost comes on the same night every year, and he's written it down.
lusk_potatoes.completion: A good row, and bigger than he put in. He looked at them a long time and gave me something from the cupboard instead. He said he'd look at the potatoes properly before he ate any.

requirements.text: The potatoes in the garden at {place:lusk}

arden_key.name: The Clock Key
arden_key.description: Mr Arden, at {place:arden}, keeps a clock on a nail to know when to stop. It stopped at nine last night. He dropped its key in the clearing going out to look at the sky, and he'd like to know when it is.
arden_key.completion: The key was in the clearing. He wound the clock and set it by the sun, and said he'd put it right at nine.

requirements.text: The clock key, in the clearing at {place:arden}

cope_shed.name: The Shed Door
cope_shed.description: Mr Cope, at {place:cope}, can't get into his shed. The door has stuck since the weekend. He asked me to put a shoulder to it. He says it was never locked. He says it has never been locked.
cope_shed.completion: The door gave on the second shove. Inside it had been swept, everywhere but a square in the middle the size of a chair. Mr Cope doesn't sweep.

requirements.text: The shed door at {place:cope}

pardew_nest.name: In the Woodpile
pardew_nest.description: Mr Pardew, at {place:pardew}, says an owl has nested in his woodpile, and he won't burn a stick of it until he knows the nest is empty. He asked me, having better knees, to look.
pardew_nest.completion: No owl. In a gap between the logs, a nest of straw, and in it three buttons off a child's coat, all alike. Mr Pardew said owls do that, and burned none of it.

requirements.text: The woodpile at {place:pardew}

voke_tea.name: His Brother's Tea
voke_tea.description: Mr Voke, at {place:voke}, has a can of tea for his brother, who cuts at {place:voke_brother}. They haven't spoken since Easter. He asked me to leave it by his brother's fire without a word said.
voke_tea.completion: I left the can by the fire. His brother didn't look up. When I came back, Mr Voke asked if he'd drunk it, and I said I didn't know, and he said that was fair.

requirements.text: The tea, by the fire at {place:voke_brother}

quayle_lodger.name: The Lodger
quayle_lodger.description: Mrs Quayle, at {place:quayle}, has a lodger who sits out in the garden in the evenings. His tea is ready and he hasn't come in. She asked me to tell him. His name is Mr Grey, she said, or was.
quayle_lodger.completion: In the garden, a cup of tea gone cold, with a skin on it, and nobody. Mrs Quayle said he'd be walking. She said he walks a great deal, now.

requirements.text: Her lodger, in the garden at {place:quayle}

hebden_water.name: From the Left
hebden_water.description: Mr Hebden, at {place:hebden}, asked me to water the seedlings in his garden. He can't carry the can any more. He said to water them from the left, the way his wife did, because they grow toward where she stood.
hebden_water.completion: I watered from the left. The seedlings in the garden all lean one way, toward the house, a little to the left of the door.

requirements.text: The seedlings in the garden at {place:hebden}

sayer_ladder.name: The Ladder
sayer_ladder.description: Mr Sayer, at {place:sayer}, lent his ladder to the family at {place:sayer_house} in the spring, to see to their roof. They never brought it back. He wants to know it's still there, and still his.
sayer_ladder.completion: The ladder was inside the walls, against the one gable left standing, freshly tarred, SAYER painted on a rung. There's no roof for it to reach. Mr Sayer said that was all right, then, and he'd fetch it on Sunday.

requirements.text: His ladder, inside the walls at {place:sayer_house}

rendle_coat.name: His Good Coat
rendle_coat.description: Mrs Rendle, at {place:rendle}, had her husband's good coat taken off the line by the lot camped at {place:rendle_camp}, off the road. She wants it back. It's the coat he's to be buried in. He's quite well, she said.
rendle_coat.completion: The coat was in the chest at their camp, folded and brushed. Mrs Rendle shook it out and held it up and said it had never been folded like that in its life.

requirements.text: The coat, in the chest at {place:rendle_camp}

treloar_bell.name: Nine O'Clock
treloar_bell.description: Mr Treloar, at {place:treloar}, says the School bell has been going early. He asked me to stand on the chalk mark in his clearing after nine, listen north, and tell him in the morning whether it went twice.
treloar_bell.completion: It went at nine, from the hill. Then again a little after, from somewhere much nearer. Mr Treloar said he knew it, and he'd set his watch by the second.

requirements.text: His clearing at {place:treloar}, after the nine o'clock bell

gethin_stump.name: Names in the Stump
gethin_stump.description: Mr Gethin, at {place:gethin}, has an old stump in his clearing that the cutters have put their names in for a hundred years. His eyes are going. He asked me to read him the newest name. Somebody cut one since Friday, he said, and nobody has been.
gethin_stump.completion: The newest cut was fresh, the wood still pale: room squared off for a name, not yet lettered, and this year. Mr Gethin said somebody was keeping a place.

requirements.text: The old stump in the clearing at {place:gethin}

ruck_kindling.name: Kindling
ruck_kindling.description: Mr Ruck, at {place:ruck}, has a bundle of kindling for the old lady at {place:ruck_cottage}, who has nobody to cut for her. He asked me to leave it at her door. She'll want to pay, and he asked me not to let her.
ruck_kindling.completion: She took the kindling through the door and pressed a bag of grapes on me and wouldn't hear no. Mr Ruck said she's done that every week for thirty years, and nobody has got away yet.

requirements.text: The kindling, to the door of {place:ruck_cottage}
